title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-04-07
content:
Attendance: Aisha, Marco, Evelyn, Samir, Lena (notes).

Purpose: Weekly perf & benchmarking sync focusing on recent latency/throughput regressions observed in customer workloads and internal stress tests.

1) Summary / high-level findings
- Observed a ~18% increase in p95 generation latency for 13B models on Dedicated pools (nvlink-connected A100s) starting 2026-04-03 after kernel update in runtime v1.9.2.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) for long-context (8k) workloads dropped ~22% in continuous-batching treadmill tests (run-117).
- Short-context (<=512) workloads largely unaffected; p50/p90 stable. Indicates regression tied to KV-cache or long-seq kernel path.

2) Repro steps and test artifacts
- Repro (internal treadmill): gs://redwood-perf/results/2026-04-07/run-117 (batching=auto, max_seq=8192, model=redwood-13B-quant, runtime=v1.9.2).
- Baseline (v1.9.0) numbers: p95=312ms (512 context), p95=1.02s (8k context).
- Current (v1.9.2) numbers: p95=1.20s (8k context), tokens/sec dropped 22%.
- CI microbench PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (contains perf harness logs).

3) Initial hypotheses
- Kernel selection change in v1.9.2 picks a different attention matmul path for long sequences causing NVLink saturation and higher cross-GPU synchronization.
- KV-cache allocation/GC path change introduced extra memcpy for large KV sizes.
- Batching heuristics interaction: new dynamic-batching thresholds cause more frequent flushes for long sequences, reducing batching efficiency.

4) Data / metrics observed
- NVLink utilization increased from ~60% to ~92% during run-117 (telemetry: infra/telemetry-export/run-117.csv).
- GPU-to-GPU memcpy time component increased by ~35ms per generate call for long contexts.
- Memory allocator logs show increased fragmentation for arena-id 3 during long-run.

5) Actions / owners (short term)
- Aisha: Add targeted microbench that toggles kernel selector flag (--force-kernel=A) and run on identical hardware to confirm kernel path impact. Due 2026-04-09. Linked: PR-842 perf additions.
- Marco: Roll forward tracing for KV-cache allocation (+detailed timestamps) and push debug build to dedicated-staging pool. Due 2026-04-08.
- Evelyn: Re-run treadmill runs with old dynamic-batching thresholds (v1.9.0 settings) to isolate batching heuristic effect. Due 2026-04-09.
- Samir: Investigate allocator fragmentation metrics and propose quick fix (increase arena size or tweak allocator strategy). Due 2026-04-12.
- Lena (SRE): Provision 2 more nodes in staging with identical nvlink topology to reproduce under higher concurrency and capture perf counters. Due 2026-04-08.

6) Longer-term / follow-ups
- If kernel path confirms regression, revert kernel selector change and schedule a canary rollback on Dedicated for one customer pool. Owner: Aisha + Release Eng. ETA: 2026-04-14 (post validation).
- Explore KV-cache memory compaction optimization (research spike by applied-ml). Owner: Samir. Deliverable: design doc. ETA: 2026-04-21.
- Add benchmark guards in CI to detect long-context p95 regressions (>10% vs baseline) and block merges. Owner: Evelyn. ETA: 2026-04-16.

7) Meeting notes / decisions
- Consensus: prioritize reproducing and isolating kernel vs KV-cache vs batching causes before rollback. Small revert on kernel selector is acceptable if we have quick validation tests.
- Do not push broad rollback to hosted-hosted clusters without canary verification.

8) Test run summary (quick logs)
- run-117 (2026-04-07): batching=auto, concurrency=32, payload=8k tokens, model=redwood-13B-quant, runtime=v1.9.2 -> p95=1.20s, tokens/sec=1,150
- baseline-run-0403: runtime=v1.9.0 -> p95=1.02s, tokens/sec=1,470
- microbench-kernel-toggle (local): forcing kernel A dropped p95 to 1.05s (prelim, needs repeat on staging nodes).

9) Open questions / unknowns
- Does this affect other model families (e.g., 7B FP16) under long context? Initial sample says no, but need broader runs.
- Is there any interaction with host-side networking stack for Dedicated pools that could amplify memcpy times?

10) Next sync
- Weekly perf sync: 2026-04-14 10:00 PT. Quick standup mid-week if Aisha or Marco finds confirmatory evidence.

Appendix: quick links
- Perf harness results: gs://redwood-perf/results/2026-04-07/run-117/
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Jira: JIRA-4823 (regression investigation)

Notes by Aisha Patel (eng-serving-runtime).
